entities.summary:
Máel Dúin mac Conaill was a king of Dál Riata in medieval Scotland, ruling from approximately 685 to 689 CE. He is believed to have succeeded his father, Áed mac Colguaill, and was known for his military campaigns against the Picts.

Máel Dúin's reign was marked by a series of battles with the Picts, who had long been a threat to the kingdoms of Scotland. Despite being outnumbered, Máel Dúin's forces emerged victorious, securing key victories at the Battle of Dal Riata and the Battle of Cennétta.

Máel Dúin's military successes were largely due to his strategic alliances with other Scottish kings and his ability to adapt to changing circumstances on the battlefield. His legacy as a skilled military leader has endured for centuries, with many historians considering him one of the most important figures in Scottish history during this period.

Despite his many accomplishments, Máel Dúin's life was cut short when he died in 689 CE at the age of approximately 45. His death marked the beginning of a new era in Scotland, as his son Áed mac Máel Dúin would go on to play a key role in shaping the country's future.

As a symbol of Scottish resistance against the Picts, Máel Dúin's legacy continues to be celebrated today, with many regarding him as a hero who fought tirelessly for his people and his land.
